newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Kabila's rebels sign major Zaire mining deal.
newsitem.headline: Kabila's rebels sign major Zaire mining deal.

text.p: Zaire's rebels, in control of the country's mineral wealth, on Wednesday signed a $1 billion deal with U.S.-based America Mineral Fields.
The company's main shareholder said AMF would buy a major copper/cobalt reclamation project, build a new zinc plant and investigate further mineral prospects in the country.

The agreement was signed by AMF's Jean-Raymonde Boulle and by financial commissioner (finance minister) Mwana Nanga Mawampanga for Laurent Kabila's rebel alliance at a ceremony in the country's second largest city and copper capital Lubumbashi.

The Kolwezi project had the potential to produce around 6,000 tonnes of cobalt and 60,000 tonnes of copper a year over the next 20 years, said Mark Collins, AMF executive vice-president for exploration.
AMF said its new zinc smelter at Kipushi would produce some 200,000 tonnes of zinc a year, 35,000 tonnes of copper and 400,000 tonnes of acid.
AMF principal shareholder Boulle said Zaire, with "fabulous yields," had the potential to be an African Chile and AMF's strategy was to get in on the ground floor.
"Our strategy as a group is to go for the highest grades and the largest deposits," he said.
Boulle said Kabila's rebels were now the de facto government in Zaire and he believed international recognition would follow the fact.

Kabila, whose rebels now control more than half of Africa's third largest country, said earlier on Wednesday he is targeting the capital Kinshasa in a bid to drive the ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko from power.
